smartphone.title: Smartphone
smartphone.subtitle: Your main camera
smartphone.text:
Modern smartphones like the vivo 200pro or Xiaomi 17 Ultra offer features that were reserved for pro cameras just years ago:

  • 4K video at up to 60fps
  • Optical Image Stabilization (OIS)
  • Pro modes for manual exposure control
  • Log profiles for color grading
  • Slow motion at 1080p/240fps

The best part: You always have it with you. The best shot is the one you can actually take.
smartphone.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Use Pro mode for manual control over ISO, shutter speed, and focus
  • Film in Log profile for more dynamic range in color grading
  • Clean the lens before every recording — fingerprints are the #1 reason for soft images
  • Save to internal storage instead of SD card for better write speeds

gimbal.title: Gimbal
gimbal.subtitle: Buttery smooth camera movement
gimbal.text:
A gimbal is the biggest quality leap you can make for under €150. It transforms shaky phone footage into cinematic motion.

Recommended models:

  • DJI OM 6 — compact, magnetic mount, ActiveTrack
  • Zhiyun Smooth 5 — more professional, heavier payload
  • Hohem iSteady X3 — budget option with solid performance

Alternative: A selfie stick with tripod function costs €15 and is enough for static shots.
gimbal.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Start with "Follow" mode for natural movement
  • Use the joystick for slow, controlled pans
  • Practice "orbit" shots: walk around an object at constant distance
  • A gimbal has no magic — slow, deliberate movements beat fast ones

stativ.title: Tripod
stativ.subtitle: Stability for every situation
stativ.text:
A tripod is essential for interviews, time-lapses, and any shot where the camera needs to stay still.

Options for every budget:

  • Joby GorillaPod — bendable legs, clamps anywhere
  • Neewer Tabletop Tripod — €20, solid quality
  • Manfrotto Compact — professional, but pricier
  • DIY — stack of books, water bottle as counterweight

On the go: Any flat surface works as a "tripod". Be creative!
stativ.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Position the tripod so you won't bump into the table
  • Use the self-timer (3s) to avoid vibrations from tapping
  • For interviews: Camera at eye level, slightly angled down
  • A small sandbag as counterweight makes lightweight tripods more stable

licht.title: Light
licht.subtitle: The most important element
licht.text:
Good light does more for your video than a more expensive camera. Bad light destroys 4K footage — good light saves 1080p footage.

Free light sources:

  • Window light — soft, natural, perfect for portraits
  • Overcast sky — natural diffusion outdoors
  • White wall — as a reflector for indirect light

Budget upgrade: A single LED panel with softbox (€30) dramatically improves your shots.
licht.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • The "golden hour" (1h after sunrise / before sunset) is magical
  • Use a white cardboard as reflector to fill harsh shadows
  • Avoid mixed lighting (daylight + tungsten) — it creates color casts
  • Backlight (rim light) separates you from the background and adds depth

power.title: Power Bank
power.subtitle: Never run out of battery again
power.text:
4K video drains batteries fast. A power bank is not a luxury — it's insurance against the worst moment: "Battery low" in the middle of your best take.

What you need:

  • At least 20,000 mAh for a shooting day
  • USB-C PD for fast charging (30W+)
  • Several short cables (0.3m) instead of one long one

Pro tip: Charge while recording — many smartphones support continuity charging.
power.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Enable "airplane mode" while shooting — saves 30% battery
  • Dim the screen to 30% during recording
  • Use a 0.3m USB-C cable — less cable clutter on the gimbal
  • Label your power bank — on set, things get mixed up
